description: The withdraw function transfers ETH to the user before updating their balance, allowing a malicious contract to reenter the function and drain the vault.
The setFeeRate function allows anyone to change the protocol fee because it is missing the onlyOwner modifier.
The changeOwner function does not prevent transferring ownership to the zero address, which could permanently lock the contract.
The contract uses raw transfer() for ERC20 tokens. If the token doesn't revert on failure and just returns false (like USDT), the contract will silently fail to transfer while still updating state.

Using tx.origin for authentication makes the contract vulnerable to phishing attacks. If the owner interacts with a malicious contract, that contract can call this function and pass the tx.origin check.
An unprotected selfdestruct function allows any user to destroy the contract and steal all held ETH.

Iterating over an array of users and sending ETH (Push pattern) can cause a Denial of Service. If one user is a smart contract that rejects ETH, the entire transaction reverts, preventing all other users from receiving funds.
The contract calculates the price of an asset using the instantaneous spot balance of a Uniswap pool. This is highly vulnerable to flash loan price manipulation.
In Solidity versions prior to 0.8.0, arithmetic operations wrap around. This contract uses 0.7.0 and does not use SafeMath, allowing an underflow to mint infinite tokens.
The swap function does not implement a deadline check. A miner or MEV bot can hold the transaction and execute it later when market conditions are unfavorable to the user (slippage/front-running).

If the SmartAccount implementation contract is left uninitialized, an attacker can initialize it and execute a transaction containing a delegatecall to a contract that executes the selfdestruct opcode. This destroys the implementation contract, freezing all functionality and funds of the wallets pointing to it.
original_contract: N/A

bug_type: Theft of funds under relaying the transaction
description: The execTransaction function refunds the relayer based on msg.data.length. An attacker can append arbitrary zero bytes to the calldata, which are cheap in gas (4 gas per byte) but refunded at a higher rate (8 gas per byte), allowing the attacker to steal funds via gas refund manipulation.
original_contract: N/A
fixed_contract:
uint256 expectedNumberOfBytes = _tx.data.length + signatures.length + 12 * 32;
uint256 dataLen = Math.min(msg.data.length, expectedNumberOfBytes);

bug_type: Attacker can gain control of counterfactual wallet
description: The counterfactual wallet address generation does not include the entrypoint address in the salt or init hash. An attacker can deploy a pre-generated wallet address using a malicious custom entrypoint, granting them full control over the wallet and its funds.
original_contract: N/A
fixed_contract: N/A

bug_type: Arbitrary transactions possible due to insufficient signature validation
description: The checkSignatures function fails to properly validate that the signer or caller is the authorized owner of the contract when processing EIP-1271 signatures. An attacker can supply a fake signer contract that always returns the EIP-1271 magic value, allowing them to execute arbitrary transactions.
original_contract: N/A
fixed_contract: N/A

bug_type: Paymaster ETH can be drained with malicious sender
description: The paymaster's validation signature lacks replay protection for user operations. A malicious user can take a previously valid sponsored signature and repeatedly execute the transaction through a modified account contract to drain the paymaster's deposit.
original_contract: N/A

bug_type: FeeRefund.tokenGasPriceFactor is not included in signed transaction data allowing the submitter to steal funds
description: The encodeTransactionData function does not include the tokenGasPriceFactor parameter in the signed safeTxHash. This allows a transaction submitter to modify the tokenGasPriceFactor after obtaining the user's signature to maliciously increase their gas repayment and steal funds.
original_contract: N/A
fixed_contract: N/A

description: The transaction nonce checks reference nonces[batchId] but do not validate the batchId itself. An attacker can replay a valid first transaction across different batches that share the same nonce value.
original_contract: N/A
fixed_contract: N/A

bug_type: Methods used by EntryPoint has onlyOwner modifier
description: The execute and executeBatch functions in SmartAccount.sol are incorrectly restricted with the onlyOwner modifier, which prevents the EntryPoint contract from successfully invoking them as part of user operations.

The implementation uses an incorrect ERC1271 magic value and function signature instead of the official standard specification, causing signature verifications with external contracts to fail or revert.
original_contract: N/A
fixed_contract: N/A

bug_type: SmartAccount.sol is intended to be upgradable but inherits from contracts that contain storage and no gaps
description: SmartAccount inherits from stateful base contracts like ModuleManager that do not contain storage gaps. Upgrading the contract or adding state variables to these base contracts can cause catastrophic storage slot collisions.
original_contract: N/A
fixed_contract: uint256[50] private __gap;
